entries.title: Verify localizes failures and Publish never runs on a dirty tree
entries.brief: Cards verify with the integration tests and repo scans they touch, Publish never verifies or pushes a dirty tree, verify is never skipped after a crash, and every agent prompt goes through a file
entries.body:
## Goal

A failing integration test stops on the card that caused it, Publish never verifies or pushes a dirty tree, and no gate is skipped after a crash.
refusal-audit stopped five times on integration-verify regressions that the plan-level verify could not localize.

## Also folded in, not in bolt before

- refusal-audit self-report 2: card `verify:` commands run package-scoped, so `cmd/lyx` repo-wide invariant scans first run at the plan level; Plan-Write could append `go test ./cmd/lyx/`.
- refusal-audit self-report 3: Webster's integration verify runs against the working tree, so an uncommitted edit can mask a non-compiling HEAD.
- Publish's conflict resolver reuses `.lyx/loom/conflict-resolution-r1.md` across Publishes (`internal/mergeresolve/spec.go:60`), so a later conflicting merge-in is refused while an earlier file exists; refusal-audit hit it.
- Deliver every agent prompt through a file, so no role can hit the 30000-byte launch limit (`internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine/command.go`); Master already does (`e39909bbc`).

## From `card-verify-integration`: Cards that touch integration-tagged tests verify with -tags integration

No refusal-audit card declared a verify: line; the fork gate is go build plus the package's unit tests (webster-body-implementer.md:30), untagged, while 11 of 48 touched test files are //go:build integration.
Want: Plan-Write adds `go test -tags integration <pkg>` to a card's verify when it touches a tagged file; a message-rewording card greps the repo for the old text first so stale exact-string assertions become part of the card; Master re-runs integration tests after a rework fork.

## From `publish-dirty-tree`: Publish must not verify or push a dirty tree after merge resolution

refusal-audit's Publish merge left historyfold_test.go uncommitted and verify ran on the dirty tree; earlier publish-review-fixback had the same uncommitted merge-resolution edits

## From `verify-gate-crash-after-merge`: Landing verify gate skips a merge interrupted before its marker write

Found reviewing PR #308 (`publish-verify-after-merge`).
Fabric reports a finished-but-interrupted merge as already up to date, so the gate cannot tell a verified tree from an unverified one.
Robust fix: record the task HEAD that last passed verify, and verify whenever HEAD differs from it.

entries.title: Clean pair lifecycle: no leftover sessions, branches, sockets or races
entries.brief: fabric remove ends the pair's tmux session, finishes half-removed pairs and deletes warp branches on origin; loom start never races a dying driver; tests stop leaking tmux sockets
entries.body:
## Goal

Removing a pair ends its tmux session first, can finish a half-removed pair, and leaves no branches, sockets or stray directories behind; starting a run never races a dying driver.

## Also folded in, not in bolt before

- After refusal-audit landed, the driver wrote a drive report into the weft; `lyx fabric remove --remote` removed the task worktree, refused the dirty weft, and a rerun answered "worktree not found", so the half-removed pair had to be finished by hand.
- Warp branches on origin (see `fabric-branch-hygiene` below): `remove --remote` deletes the weft branch on origin but never the warp branch, and squash merges mean git never sees them as merged.
  On 2026-10-02 the hub deleted 37 such warp branches by hand (no open PR, no live pair).
  Want: `remove --remote` deletes the warp branch on origin too, and `fabric cleanup --remote` finds warp branches on origin with no live pair and no open PR.

## From `fabric-remove-ends-reed-session`: fabric remove leaves the pair tmux session alive

Seen 2026-09-30 for quarry-cli-answers and status-strand-by-driver: after landing and `fabric remove --remote`, their reed sessions were still alive hours later.
A driver that wrote its stop report after the removal recreated `<hub>/<slug>/.lyx/...` and `<hub>/<slug>/_lyx/shed/<slug>/drive-reports/<report>.md`: a stray directory, and a drive report that never reached the archive.
The hub killed the sessions and deleted the dirs by hand.

Fix: remove (and batten teardown) ends the pair reed session (reed down) before deleting the worktrees, and waits for or refuses on a live driver; a stop report written after done should land before the archive tag.

## From `driver-restart-race`: loom start races the ly-drive self-removal and ends with no driver

After a hand-back, the ly-drive session removes its own strand with a detached `lyx reed remove --name loom-driver --detach` that waits for the session's pid to exit (end-of-session command from `083e992cf`).
A `lyx loom start` issued in that window sees the loom-driver strand still live, keeps it instead of spawning a driver, and the detached remover then deletes it: the run is left with no driver and nothing happens (hit on `batten-hub-ready` and `focus-marker-warn`, 2026-09-30; a second `loom start` works).
Fix direction: `loom start` treats a driver strand with a pending self-removal (or whose claude has exited) as gone and spawns a fresh one, or the remover skips a strand that was re-adopted since it was scheduled.

## From `batten-resume-sees-stale-blocked`: batten run right after loom start exits on the child's stale blocked state

Seen 2026-09-30 on batten-records-leak-into-pairs: after a hub fix, `lyx loom start --no-attach` (ok) followed at once by `lyx batten run` ended with Run-Shed "inner shed run reached state blocked" because status.json still said blocked for a few seconds.
Fix direction: loom start writes state running (or a resume marker) before returning, or batten treats a blocked child whose driver was just relaunched as running.

## From `fabric-branch-hygiene`: Fabric: branches left behind by a failed add and on the remote

Read the closed GitHub issues #269 (add rollback leaves the warp branch) and #270 (cleanup cannot see weft branches stranded on the remote). Re-check both once `landing` has landed: it takes #293 (remove leaves the warp branch, locally and on origin), which touches the same branch-lifecycle code, and the ly-drive may repair the rest from a trace.

After `landing` (#298): `fabric remove` now deletes the local warp branch, but `--remote` still deletes only the weft branch on origin; warp branches of removed pairs stay there (`board-done-on-landing`, `burler-exclude-warn`, `integration-verify-fence`, `loom-start-layout`, `stencil-drift-remedy`, `stuck-reason-in-status`, `landing`). Out of scope in landing's decision record.

## From `main-weft-not-pushed`: main-weft is never pushed and never advances on landing

Seen 2026-09-30, uninvestigated: the prime weft branch main-weft stays local and does not move when a task lands

## From `test-tmux-socket-leak`: Integration tests leave tmux sockets behind

Tests leak tmux sockets: `/tmp/tmux-1000/` holds hundreds of `lyx-Test…`, `lyx-contract-…` and `lyx-warp-bare-…` sockets left by reed/loom integration tests. Test fixtures should kill their tmux server and remove the socket in `t.Cleanup`.

entries.title: PATTERN for loomyard, plus repo conventions
entries.brief: CONSTRAINTS.md becomes _lyx/PATTERN.md so agents get the constraints directive; warp/weft scan beyond Go code; model specs in short form; ide workspace cleanups
entries.body:
## Goal

loomyard gets `_lyx/PATTERN.md` so lyx agents receive the constraints directive, which no run has received so far; CONSTRAINTS.md moves there.
Runs alone, last: it repoints CONSTRAINTS.md in ~130 files.

## Also folded in

- `fabric-vocabulary-everywhere`, `model-spec-short-form` and `ide-hub-workspace-followups` below.
- `model-spec-short-form`'s model trial (`fable[high]` for discussion and review) moved to `convergence-plan`, where it is measured; this task does only the short form, the dead link and Master's explicit effort.

## From `pattern-init`: Initialize PATTERN for loomyard: CONSTRAINTS.md becomes _lyx/PATTERN.md

Operator 2026-10-01: CONSTRAINTS.md is millhouse's setup; loomyard's variant is PATTERN, not yet initialized.
Verified: no _lyx/PATTERN.md in loomyard-weft, and there is no init verb. internal/pattern injects a role directive (implementer, review-fix, orchestrator) pointing at _lyx/PATTERN.md into webster fork/Master, burler and loom plan prompts only when the file exists, so today's runs got no PATTERN directive (they only saw CONSTRAINTS.md through CLAUDE.md and stencil mentions).
Work: move CONSTRAINTS.md's invariants into _lyx/PATTERN.md (weft, invisible to the code repo; optionally split under _lyx/pattern/); repoint everything that names CONSTRAINTS.md: CLAUDE.md, stencils (loom discussion/plan/rework, webster master and prefix-recovery), the ly-drive skill, contracts/specs, burlercli/run.go, loomshed and treadleengine docs, and contracts/stencils/citation_enforcement_test.go; decide whether a `lyx pattern init` verb is wanted for other repos.

## From `fabric-vocabulary-everywhere`: Fabric vocabulary: warp and weft only inside fabric, also in docs, specs and tests

Operator 2026-09-30: warp and weft are fabric-internal words; nothing outside fabric should know them.
Seen on refusal-audit: contracts/specs/refusal-spec.md and several _test.go files outside fabric use them, and the scan let them through.
Want: extend the scan to contracts/, docs/, manifest/, plugins/ skills and test files outside the owner set (or an explicit allowlist for fabric docs), and sweep the existing hits.

## From `model-spec-short-form`: Model specs in the short form everywhere, and per-role model choice revisited

Seen 2026-10-01: long form in internal/loomengine/template.yaml (discussion, plan, review, friction), internal/websterengine/template.yaml (recovery), internal/landingshed/template.yaml (conflict, describe) and contracts/specs/llm-model-spec.md's examples; the spec only mentions in one sentence that a bare bracket token means effort. Template comments cite docs/reference/model-spec.md, which is missing; the spec lives at contracts/specs/llm-model-spec.md.
Webster master is plain `sonnet`, so its effort (medium) comes invisibly from models.yaml; write it explicitly.
Model choice (operator, 2026-10-01): try `fable[high]` for discussion and review, where design judgement matters (refusal-audit's holes came from opus Discussion and opus reviews; a Fable review found the design problem), keep sonnet for implementation; change it only between runs and measure review rounds, PR rejects and interventions before and after (convergence-plan).

## From `ide-hub-workspace-followups`: ide hub workspace: review follow-ups

Follow-ups from the PR #301 review (`85902381e`), all non-blocking:
- `internal/fabricengine/hubworkspace.go` builds the prime path by hand (`filepath.Join(l.HubPath, primeName, l.AnchorRel)`) instead of `WorktreePath`.
- `internal/ideengine/spawn.go` now WARNs on every spawn whose prime resolution fails, task spawns included (silent before).
- Removing the last pair prunes `_portals/<anchor>`, so the hub workspace shows a missing folder until the next prime spawn.
- Relative-path settings spliced from the prime into the workspace file resolve against `_launchers/`, not the prime.

## From `manifest-to-bolt`: Move everything in manifest/ into bolt and retire the folder

Operator 2026-10-01: LYXHUB takes over all development of loomyard; everything in manifest/ goes into bolt.
The operator also says much of it is outdated: triage each roadmap Someday item with the operator (keep as tier 3 or tier 2, merge, or strike) and carry its designs/<name>.md over as the bolt entry's design doc.

entries.title: Review convergence: the judge decides converged, continue or circling from fresh reviews
entries.brief: The Bouncer judge stops reviewing the artifacts and judges convergence from facts Go hands it (counts, severities, trend, reopened ledger keys), on its own sonnet[medium] key; at least one fresh round, circling escalates; plus finding classes
entries.body:
## Goal

A review segment stops when it has converged, judged from fresh reviews, and escalates when it circles.
Today the Bouncer judge is a second reviewer: `contracts/stencils/bouncer/bouncer-template-judge.md` opens with "You are a review-gate judge: a reviewer of the target artifacts against the rubric", reads the artifacts first, and `internal/shedadapters/bouncer.go` maps its APPROVED straight to Done.
So "every finding fixed" counts as converged, although the fixes are new text no fresh reviewer has seen.
The prompt is wrong by design, not the agent: it does what it is told (operator, 2026-10-02).

## Seen in rework-generations (2026-10-02)

One Discussion-Burler round found four MEDIUM, two LOW and two NIT; the fixer fixed all eight, three of them new design decisions; the judge checked each fix against the decision record, marked all resolved, and the segment ended without a second fresh review.
With a high-temperature reviewer every round is a new sample, and one sample cannot show convergence.

## Shape

- The judge's role is the operator's: a quick sit-rep agent that decides converged, continue or circling, and does not itself read the artifacts or the code.
- The judge decides all three outcomes; a pure mechanical rule was considered and rejected (operator, 2026-10-02): severities are the reviewer's own noisy labels, a nitpicky MEDIUM would force rounds up to `max_bounces`, and a reworded old finding looks new.
- Go hands the judge the facts instead of the artifacts: per round, the finding count and highest severity (and class, once findings carry one), the trend across rounds, and which ledger keys were reopened.
- Only two things stay mechanical: at least one fresh Burler round before convergence is possible (the seed entry has no fresh review, so it never converges straight away), and `max_bounces` as the upper bound.
- Fixed findings never count as convergence on their own; the fixes are new text, and the judge weighs whether the latest fresh review still found MEDIUM-or-worse.
- Circling escalates to the operator.
- The judge gets its own model key: today it shares loom's `review` key (`opus[effort=high]` in `internal/loomengine/template.yaml`) with the reviewers, which is part of why it acts as one; `judge: sonnet[medium]` (operator: Sonnet 5.5 is fast and cheap now, and the job is narrow).
- Applies to all three review segments (Discussion-, Plan- and Webster-Review).
- The reviewer's own top verdict (`verdict: APPROVED` with MEDIUM findings) mixes "not blocking" with "converged"; the judge must not read it as converged.
## Finding classes (from manifest/designs/review-finding-classification.md)

- Add a finding-class field (`design`, `scope`, `decision`, `consistency`) to burler's review contract and the rubrics; `internal/burlerengine/verdict.go` has only severity today.
- End the round loop when a round returns zero gating-class findings, keeping the cap as a backstop.
- Emit per-class counts in the round record, so the same class recurring across rounds is visible.
- Add a line to the Review Round Invariant: class decides who decides and when the loop stops, never whether a finding is fixed.

entries.title: Prompt-cache TTL per agent role
entries.brief: Parked: workers on 5m cache TTL, waiting sessions on 1h — operator deciding
entries.body:
Claude Code gives a subscription's main session a 1-hour prompt-cache TTL (cache write 2× base input) and subagents/forks 5 minutes (1.25×); every lyx agent is a main session in tmux, so all of them write at the 1-hour price (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching.md).

Measured on the `landing` run's transcripts: Discussion, Plan, Bouncer and Burler never paused more than 90 s between turns, so 5 minutes keeps them warm; ly-drive paused up to 508 s (three gaps over 5 minutes), so it needs 1 hour. Webster Master waits on forks via Monitor and is not yet measured.

Likely shape: shuttle sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m|1h` (Claude Code v2.1.242+) per role when it spawns a session, configurable per role. loomyard was developed with the 5-minute limit in mind, so 5 minutes matches its design assumption.

entries.title: Convergence: measure hub and driver interventions, fix at the source, hardening freezes
entries.brief: Plan for lyx to converge rather than accumulate bugs: per-run intervention log, real-wiring tests, feature freezes
entries.body:
Operator 2026-09-30: take a step back and plan for convergence, not keep accepting more bugs.
Observed today: nearly every hub intervention was in same-day new code (#319: approve nil dep, reject reading its file argument as run-id), and both passed tests built on fake deps.
Ingredients: (1) log every hub intervention and ly-drive repair per run with a class and cause, so interventions per run and new-vs-repeat failure classes are visible; (2) every fix at the source with a test that drives the real CLI wiring, not only fakes; (3) freeze periods with no new verbs or recipe rows, hardening only, until the intervention rate flattens.
Goal: the outside LLM steps in rarely, and for the task rather than for lyx.
## Model trial (from `model-spec-short-form`, operator 2026-10-01)

Try `fable[high]` for discussion and review, where design judgement matters (refusal-audit's holes came from opus Discussion and opus reviews; a Fable review found the design problem), and keep sonnet for implementation.
Change it only between runs, and measure review rounds, PR rejects and interventions before and after.

entries.title: An MCP server over lyx exposing the verbs agents need
entries.brief: A few coarse MCP tools over lyx, chosen by measured agent use and exposed per role, so agents see typed schemas instead of guessing CLI shapes
entries.body:
## Why

Agents misuse or bypass lyx (the hub read `_board/*.json` with jq) because the CLI shape is not discoverable.
An MCP tool carries a typed input schema and a description.

## Constraint from the operator (2026-10-01)

Not one tool per verb: MCP entries are heavy.
Only the important ones are exposed, and how to pick them is still open.

## Proposed selection

1. **Measure first.** Mine transcripts and logs for which lyx commands agents run, where they fail, and where they read around lyx.
2. **Few coarse tools.** One tool per area with an `action` enum (the pattern of Claude Code's Artifact tool), e.g. `board`, `run` (status, approve, reject), `webster` (Master only); a handful in total.
3. **Per-role exposure.** A fork may get none, Master gets `webster`, the hub gets `board` and `run`.

## Shape

- A thin server shipped in the ly plugin; each action calls the same module seam the CLI uses, so behaviour never forks.
- The CLI stays for humans and scripts.
- Wins: no shell-quoted JSON payloads, and per-tool permissions (an agent can be denied `accept-audit`).

Related: `bolt-roadmap-tiers`, `process-naming`.


## Status: needs a careful design session first

Operator 2026-10-01: what goes into the MCP must be thought through very carefully; this is not a loom task yet.
Questions for that session:

- Which verbs need an MCP tool at all, and which are served well enough by a better `--help` (payload schema and an example per command) and a per-role command card in each stencil, generated from the cobra tree?
- Is permission gating (an agent denied `accept-audit` or `approve`) the real reason for MCP, since `--help` and cards cannot give it?
- One tool per module was raised and judged too heavy (long descriptions); what is the cut instead?

entries.title: Discussion advisor: a dedicated agent answers Discussion-Write's questions live
entries.brief: A second agent spawned beside Discussion-Write studies the task and code and answers its design questions as they arise, a real two-agent dialogue
entries.body:
- **ask mode**: Discussion-Write asks its design questions as they arise, and an answerer replies; answers to design questions, not a review.
- **The answerer is a dedicated agent**, spawned in parallel with Discussion-Write with its own prompt: it studies the task, bolt and the code while the writer drafts, so it is ready when the questions come.
  It is an address, not hard-wired to `$LYX_PARENT`; the parent is the fallback.
- Two live sessions both keep their context, so this is a real dialogue, and none of it lands in the parent's context.
  Two agents designing together beat one agent asking and answering itself.
- `ask` and `review` are independent switches: an advisor answering interview questions and the parent reviewing the draft can both run on one task.
- New machinery: one producer running two interactive sessions side by side (e.g. `ly:<slug>:discussion` and `ly:<slug>:advisor`), each waiting on the other through files; shuttle keeps an asking session non-terminal today (`internal/shuttleengine/wait.go`), which is the starting point.

entries.title: Plan cards name the members they change as glyphs, after the glyph library is tested properly
entries.brief: Plan-Write lists file paths instead of member glyphs because its stencil shows and allows it, and handle-unreferenced forces invented glyphs; test the glyph library at scale first
entries.body:
## Why

Seen on `gate-list`'s plan (2026-10-02): card 1's `Edit:` lists 24 file paths and no member glyph, although its Intent names the members it changes (`GateSpec`, `GateOutcome`, `Run.evaluateGate`, `resolveGateSpec`, `burlerengine#Engine.Run`).
Webster's changed-files guard then compares at file level only, no `quarry resolve` confirms the members exist, and a kick-start pack (`kick-start-pack`) has no spans to pre-resolve.

## Causes, in `contracts/stencils/loom/loom-template-plan.md`

- The only card skeleton shows `**Edit:**` with `` - `path/to/file.go` ``, and agents copy the shape they are shown.
- The glyph rule says a *symbol* target is spelled as a glyph and "a file path stays a plain path"; nothing says an `Edit` target should be the members changed, so a file path is always a legal choice.
- File paths are the path of least resistance: a member glyph must be looked up with `lyx quarry` and resolve at validation, and can fail as `glyph-not-found`, `glyph-ambiguous` or `containment-unit-overlap`; a file path only has to exist.
- `handle-unreferenced` requires every `plan:` handle to be used by a later card, so a new symbol only its own card uses cannot take a handle; the planner then invents a glyph (`internal/shuttleengine#GateEntry` under `Create:`), which the handle rule exists to prevent.

## Want

- The skeleton and the text say `Edit:` lists the member glyphs changed; a file path only for a file with no symbol to name (tests, non-Go files).
- The plan rubric flags an `Edit` card holding only file paths while its Intent names specific symbols.
- `handle-unreferenced` does not fire for a handle its own declaring card uses.

## First: test the glyph library properly (operator, 2026-10-02)

The operator is not sure loomyard's glyph library works in practice: it is tested through crucible, not through real plans at scale.
Pushing planners onto member glyphs makes every plan depend on it, so before the stencil change, exercise it against real plans: resolve every member glyph a sample of real cards would name, the handle bind path, and the containment checks, and record what fails.

## Validation must not change verdict mid-run (2026-10-02)

Seen on `rework-generations`, batch 5: a plan valid at Plan-Write was refused at `begin-batch` with `containment-file-overlap`.
Card 4 creates `loomshed#ReworkTold` with a `plan:` handle; card 5 lists both `internal/loomshed/prrework.go` and `loomshed#ReworkTold`; card 9 lists `prrework.go`.
While the unit did not exist the handle had no location, so containment could not place it; once card 4 built it and `begin-batch` canonicalized the handle into a glyph, containment saw the overlap for the first time.
Cards 5 and 9 sit in different, sequential batches, so the overlap was harmless; the member line in card 5 was redundant beside its own file line.

Want: validation gives the same answer at Plan-Write and at dispatch.
Either containment places a `plan:` handle by its declared file at plan time, or it does not refuse overlaps between cards in different batches; and a card listing a file and a member of that same file is flagged at plan time as redundant.

entries.title: Webster recovers from a re-begin, its own canonicalization and an integration regression
entries.brief: Fix #329, #330, #332: only landed batches count as built, webster's own card rewrites update their hashes, forks fix what their card broke and a bisected regression gets a recovery fork
entries.body:
## Goal

A webster run recovers on its own from the three states that today need a hand edit or a human: a re-begun batch, its own plan canonicalization, and an integration regression.

## Bugs

- #329: a re-begun batch whose fork landed nothing is validated as if its cards were built, so later cards that Use its Create targets are refused.
- #330: `rebaseline` refuses begun cards that `begin-batch` canonicalized itself, because the recorded card hashes keep the pre-canonical text.
- #332: an integration regression bisected to a card ends the run as `blocked` with no fix attempt, although the batch forks had seen the failures.

## Fix direction

- #329: only a batch that landed commits counts as built; a begun batch with nothing landed validates like a first begin.
- #330: when webster rewrites a begun card, it updates that card's recorded hash in the same step, so its own edits never count as drift.
- #332: a batch fork that sees a test its own card broke fixes it before reporting done.
  An integration regression bisected to a card gets a recovery fork against that card before the run escalates.

## Done when

- Each issue's "Seen" scenario has a regression test that passes.
- CLAUDE.md's TEMPORARY items for #329, #330 and #332 are deleted (the issues are already closed into this task).

entries.title: A run's parent is the worktree it is seeded from; batten survives pauses; parent-review loops
entries.brief: Fix #341, #338: parent from the seeding worktree, batten waits through paused/blocked, parent-review reviews every rewrite up to a cap
entries.body:
## Goal

A run knows its parent from where it was seeded, and batten carries a run through pauses instead of dying, so a run needs no special shell, environment variable or restart to reach the orch session.

## Bugs

- #341: a run's `parent` is the caller's `LYX_STRAND_NAME`, so a run started from a plain shell has no parent and its escalations reach no one.
- #338: a paused or blocked inner run makes `lyx batten run` exit `failed`, leaving no watcher to land or tear down the pair.

## Fix direction

- #341: creating and seeding a pair records the worktree it is seeded from as `parent`.
  A driver that messages upward resolves the orch session running in that worktree.
  This rewrites the Agent Name Invariant in `CONSTRAINTS.md` in the same commit.
  Open for Discussion: what a message does when the parent worktree has no orch session (queue until one appears, or log only).
- #338: batten waits through `paused` and `blocked`, tells the parent once, and carries on when the run is `running` again.
- Parent-review gets more than one round: today `attempts: 1` with `pass_on_cap: true` lets the rewrite after a reject through unseen.
  The parent reviews each rewrite until it approves, up to a cap Discussion sets, and escalates at the cap instead of passing.

## Done when

- A run started with plain `lyx batten run <slug>` from the prime has the prime as parent, and its parent-review request reaches the orch session.
- Pausing and resuming an inner run leaves its batten watcher alive.
- A rejected discussion comes back to the parent for review until approved or the cap escalates.
- CLAUDE.md's TEMPORARY items for #341 and #338 are deleted (the issues are already closed into this task).

entries.title: Deploy and VS Code leave every worktree runnable and clean
entries.brief: Fix #339, #340, #334: defaulted keys are not required, reed sizes to the latest client and folder-open spares the orch strand, ide spawn writes .git/info/exclude
entries.body:
## Goal

Deploying lyx and opening worktrees in VS Code leave every worktree runnable and clean, with no manual step after either.

## Bugs

- #339: a new required config key shipped by a deploy makes loom refuse in every worktree until `lyx config reconcile --apply` runs there.
- #340: opening the prime in VS Code while `lyx orch` hosts the hub collapses the orch pane to 3 rows and stalls every cycle.
- #334: `lyx ide spawn` writes a lyx-managed block into a task pair's tracked `.gitignore`.

## Fix direction

- #339: a key that has a default is not required: loom fills a missing key from its default and logs it instead of refusing.
- #340: reed sizes its sessions to the latest client (`window-size latest`), and the folder-open task skips `reed add` when the worktree already has an orch strand.
- #334: `lyx ide spawn` records its ignore in `.git/info/exclude`, never in a tracked `.gitignore`.
  Rename the repo `.gitignore`'s "mill-managed" block, now that mill is gone.

## Done when

- A deploy that adds a defaulted key leaves running pairs runnable with no reconcile.
- Opening the prime in VS Code leaves the orch pane's size and session alone.
- `lyx ide spawn` on a pair leaves `git status` clean.
- CLAUDE.md's TEMPORARY items for #339, #340 and #334 are deleted (the issues are already closed into this task).

entries.title: Webster's strand is named webster, and each module names its agents with its own constant
entries.brief: Webster's orchestrating strand shows as <sn>:<slug>:master because its model-config key doubles as its strand role; give it the role webster, and every spawn site takes its role from a constant in its own module
entries.body:
## Goal

An operator reading `lyx reed list` sees each agent named for what it is.

## Today

- `internal/agentname` forms `<shortname>[:<slug>]:<role>`, and each spawning module passes its own role, mostly as an inline literal in its spawn spec.
- Webster spawns its orchestrating session with `string(RoleMaster)` (`internal/websterengine/runlevel.go`), the same value that keys its model in `webster.yaml`, so the strand shows as `...:master`.

## Fix direction

- Webster's orchestrating strand gets the role `webster`, separate from its model key; whether the `master` model key in `webster.yaml` is renamed too is for Discussion, and a rename must keep existing configs loading.
- Each module keeps owning the roles it spawns: the role is a named constant in that module, beside its spawn site, not an inline literal.
  There is no central role list; `agentname`'s role set stays open, so a new module with its own agent touches no shared file.

## Done when

- A webster run's orchestrating strand is named `<shortname>:<slug>:webster`.
- Every spawn site takes its role from a named constant in its own module.
- The Agent Name Invariant in `CONSTRAINTS.md` states that the spawning module owns its role, and CLAUDE.md's Merriam terminology entry stays accurate.

## Depends on

`webster-recovery` (both edit `internal/websterengine`) and `run-parentage` (both edit how agent names are formed and the Agent Name Invariant).
